name: nbody
axis: realistic whole program: f64 arithmetic over an array of mutable structs (O(n^2) pairwise force loop over 5 bodies)
notes: Adapted from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game `nbody` (Mark C. Lewis' 5-body shape); the physics, the constants and the 0.01 timestep are the reference program's. TWO deliberate adaptations: (1) all four languages print through the SAME integer-scaling `fmt9` (trunc(|v|*1e9+0.5), then sign + integer part + '.' + 9 zero-padded digits) instead of each runtime's printf/toFixed, so the four outputs are byte-identical by construction and no formatting library sits inside the measurement; (2) VL's i64->string renderer is written out longhand in main.vl instead of `import { toStr } from "std:fmt"` because that import makes the module fail to EMIT (see vlLimitations: 'object literal matches no union variant'). All four agree bit-for-bit at n=1000 with the published benchmarks-game reference output (-0.169075164 / -0.169087605). Scale-verified: rust 0.755->1.494s, deno 1.500->2.504s, VL 1.456->2.904s, python 0.604->1.172s across 25M->50M (250k->500k for python). Python's N is 1/100. Final timings (min over all observations, min-of-N wall clock, pinned to rotating P-cores): rust 1.494s, deno 2.504s, VL 2.904s (prebuilt module; 1.94x Rust, 1.16x deno), python(500k) 1.172s. `vl build -O3` REGRESSES this one: 2.994s plain vs 3.293s at -O3 over min-of-5.
